subject: Figure AI humanoid robots deployed at BMW's Spartanburg plant

framework: Norman's Gap (ownership at the reception point)

situation: Everyone touches this problem but nobody actually owns fixing it.

framework: Escalation Architecture (who appoints, who scopes, who receives)

subject: KPMG Australia CEO and audit head resign after two self-run investigations cleared the firm and a third, independent one didn't

framework: Norman's Law (load-bearing constraint breaking) / Resignable List

framework: Standing Tradeoff Outliving Its Governance Level

framework: The Two-Clock Reconciliation Gate (truth clock vs. pressure clock)

framework: Message Divergence (internal truth vs. external message)

framework: Clock Reconciliation (capital-markets clock vs. engineering clock)

framework: Stakes-Migration Trigger (decision rights and the altitude of the call)

framework: Norman's Law (a system optimized for one variable fails at every other under load)

framework: Norman's Law (proximity to a broken system reduces the capacity to see it)

tags: Leadership; Decision Quality; Internal Regulation
subject: Market skepticism about insider CEO Fiddelke gets priced in ahead of his first Target earnings print

situation: I think a decision already got made somewhere before it reached my desk.

tags: Norman's Law; Decision Quality; Management Operating System
subject: Synthesis: Meta layoffs + Lululemon CEO search + Meta age-verification + Varda/pharma + Banks resignation
summary: Five industries, one inversion: in every case the room believed it was deciding when the decision had already been made upstream by a spec, a capex line, or a hold nobody named.

framework: Norman's Gap (holding a personnel call under live political pressure)

tags: Leadership; Internal Regulation; Organizational Behavior
subject: Border Patrol Chief Michael Banks resigns after weeks of misconduct reporting, framed as a 'second retirement'

framework: Norman's Law (consensus-optimized systems can't produce commercial velocity)
situation: A competitor just did something we've called 'not practical' for years.
action: Check whether a private vendor has priced a capability your team has dismissed for a decade. If yes and no procurement file exists, book the meeting.
tags: Decision Quality; Operational Excellence; Management Operating System
subject: Startup Varda turns a 25-year ISS research capability into a paid commercial service for United Therapeutics
summary: Same physics, different operating system: incumbent pharma routed microgravity manufacturing through R&D review for over a decade while a 2020 startup priced it as a vendor invoice.

situation: We're building more compliance or audit infrastructure than the regulator actually asked for.

tags: AI and Technology; Internal Regulation; Operational Excellence

summary: The regulator specified an outcome (keep under-13s off the platform); Meta built a biometric inference layer across 2.5 billion users — an order of magnitude past what was required.

framework: Norman's Gap (the spec decides the hire before the first interview)
situation: We're searching for a new hire and I'm worried the job spec already picked the answer.
action: Read your senior-role job spec's first paragraph aloud. If your customer can't recognize their experience in it, rewrite it before end of day.
tags: Leadership; Decision Quality; Management Operating System
subject: Lululemon's stock falls 13% on the CEO announcement after a 300-day search
summary: The board solved for a legible, defensible résumé instead of the creative-cadence problem the brand actually had — the outcome was locked the moment the job spec was written.

framework: Signal Compression / Norman's Law (narrative substitution under capex pressure)
situation: We're calling a financial decision a strategic one and I'm not sure that's honest.
action: Find one decision your team is calling 'strategic' that's actually structural. Name the real driver out loud, in the next meeting.
tags: Decision Quality; Internal Regulation; Management Operating System
subject: Meta cuts 8,000 jobs at a record-revenue company, framed as an AI productivity move
summary: The CFO named the layoffs as a capex offset on the earnings call; the AI-pod reorg was cover for a financing decision, not the cause of one.

framework: Norman's Gap (identity fusion to the seat)
situation: A founder or executive won't separate themselves from the role, and it's costing us.
action: Write a one-page behavior gate with your chair: meetings you won't take, customers who escalate past you, appearances that need sign-off.
tags: Leadership; Internal Regulation; Organizational Behavior
subject: Fermi America's valuation falls from $20B to $3.4B; customer conversations accelerate the day the CEO is removed
summary: Six months of behavioral warning signs were filed by the board as 'political noise' and 'supply chain reality' instead of being read as the same signal: the CEO was the friction.

framework: Norman's Gap (substrate decisions delegated as if they were tool decisions)
situation: I don't know if our AI vendor choice is a small decision or a five-year commitment.
action: Block 30 minutes: where AI is entering your workflows, your priced switching cost in 24 months, and who has renewal leverage over you. Owner: the CEO seat.
tags: AI and Technology; Decision Quality; Leadership
subject: Anthropic-PE joint venture, OpenAI's Development Company, and Apple's model-picker land in the same 72 hours
summary: Three announcements read individually as product news; together they show the AI distribution layer hardening into an oligopoly while most companies still route the question to the CIO.

situation: We're about to announce a big hire or launch and I'm not sure the structure behind it is real.
action: Before the announcement goes out, write the authority surface, named owner, integration cadence, and trigger that would change it.
tags: AI and Technology; Decision Quality; Internal Regulation
subject: UBTECH advertises an $18M Chief Scientist role with no defined authority, against a mounting net loss
summary: Hardware production scaled 20x while the intelligence layer didn't; the seven-figure hire announcement was a public confession of the gap, not a fix for it.

framework: Norman's Law (decision abdication distributed across a board)
situation: We keep discussing a declining number every quarter and nothing changes.
action: Pick the metric that's slipped for two-plus quarters. Write the threshold, named owner, 90-day mandate, and board reporting cadence today.
tags: Decision Quality; Leadership; Internal Regulation
subject: Target's slow quarterly review cadence let four years of share loss compound into a $5B turnaround
summary: The data reached every quarterly deck from 2022 on; what never reached the agenda was the question of whether the decision cycle itself was too slow to compete.

framework: Norman Decision Time (the gap between knowing and acting)
situation: I keep seeing warning signs but nobody acts until it's too late.
action: Name the most important decision your operation is running on. Ask whether the information behind it is real or already shaped, compressed, or assumed.
tags: Norman's Law; Signal Quality; Decision Quality
subject: Synthesis: Pentagon intel-briefing leak + PIF/LIV Golf + AI escalation + Spirit Airlines + neurodivergent misread
summary: Five unrelated failures in one week shared one variable: not the event, not the system, but the gap between when each leader knew and when they acted.

situation: I'm about to put a high performer on a performance plan and something feels off.
action: Name the person you've been reading as a performance problem. Ask what they see or catch that the team structurally can't, before you act.
tags: Leadership; Organizational Behavior; Internal Regulation
subject: A neurodivergent high performer is put on a performance plan for meeting attendance, not output
summary: A single-channel performance-reading system compressed a contributor's early risk-catches and hard deliverables into 'communication style concerns.'

framework: Norman's Gap (interpretation failure, not information failure)
situation: I know a strategy isn't working anymore but I keep running it anyway.
action: Name the one input your system depends on but doesn't control. Write what happens if it moves 50% in 60 days, and assign an owner to the stress test.
tags: Operational Excellence; Decision Quality; External Pressure
subject: Spirit Airlines liquidates after a fuel-price shock exposes an already-dead cost-advantage strategy
summary: The cost-advantage thesis died in 2023 when legacy carriers matched Spirit's pricing; the fuel shock just removed the ability to keep delaying the admission.

situation: My team acts on AI-generated summaries without checking what got left out.
action: Compare your last AI-generated summary to its raw source. If a conditional or threshold flag didn't survive the compression, name the gap and assign an owner.
tags: Signal Quality; AI and Technology; Decision Quality
subject: AI-generated pre-reads compress signal with no escalation check for what's omitted
summary: A clean AI summary read a conditional supplier-risk flag as resolved; the escalation architecture had no protocol for catching what synthesis leaves out.

situation: One of my biggest customers, suppliers, or funders might be about to walk, and I don't have a plan.
action: Name your top supplier, customer, and funder as percentages. Assign one owner to answer: what would we do tomorrow if any of them left?
tags: Internal Regulation; External Pressure; Decision Quality
subject: Saudi PIF withdraws funding from LIV Golf after 3 years and billions committed
summary: Six prior PIF portfolio cancellations were each read as isolated logistics; together they were the pattern that predicted the LIV withdrawal months in advance.
